progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: From C08: a weak acid ionises partly; the ICE table (c, 0, 0; −x, +x, +x; c − x, x, x); Ka = x²/(c − x); drop x when Ka is tiny next to c, so x = √(Ka × c); check x ÷ c under 5%, a rule of thumb; if the check fails, solve the full equation; x has the significant figures of Ka, so pH has that many decimal places. From C10: [H₃O⁺] = 10⁻ᵖᴴ; the table run backwards ([A⁻] = [H₃O⁺], [HA] = c − [H₃O⁺]) needs no 5% check, because [H₃O⁺] is measured; pKa = −log Ka, with two decimal places for a two-significant-figure Ka; pH describes a solution and Ka describes the acid; Ka × Kb = Kw for a conjugate pair. From C06: amphiprotic species give or take a proton depending on the partner; the proton chains H₂CO₃, HCO₃⁻, CO₃²⁻ and H₃PO₄, H₂PO₄⁻, HPO₄²⁻, PO₄³⁻; NaHCO₃ and KH₂PO₄ dissolve to give the amphiprotic anion with a spectator cation. From Module 5 (chem-m5-c06b): "multiply both sides by the bottom, then divide" for rearranging. Mathematics: the quadratic formula (Mathematics Advanced). For students without it, the formula line on screen shows every substituted value, and the substitution check confirms the root. Not assumed: buffers, salt hydrolysis, half-equivalence.
progression.startsWith: Unseen weak-acid data. The video opens: Weak acid questions give you different data, and the data choose the method.
progression.stopsAfter: calculating the pH of a weak acid with the shortcut and justifying it with the 5% check; recognising a failed check, solving the full equation for x and comparing the result with the shortcut; calculating Ka and pKa from a measured pH and concentration, with no 5% check because [H₃O⁺] is measured, and explaining why pKa is not the pH; writing the equations for HCO₃⁻ and H₂PO₄⁻ reacting with water as an acid and as a base, and deciding which way each mainly reacts with water by comparing its Ka with its Kb from the acid one proton up, and predicting whether solutions of NaHCO₃ and KH₂PO₄ are basic or acidic.
progression.nextLesson: how a buffer resists a change in pH (route chem-m6-c11).

teaching.task: A weak acid question gives you a Ka, a measured pH, or an ion that can go either way. Which method fits those data, and how do you check the answer?
teaching.causalExplanation: Why x can be dropped in Q1: Ka is tiny next to c, so very little ionises (2b), confirmed by the check (2c). Why the shortcut fails in Q2: about a quarter of the acid ionises, so c − x is nowhere near c (3b). Why the full equation is needed and which root to keep (3c). Why [A⁻] equals [H₃O⁺] when working backwards: each molecule that ionises makes one of each (4b). Why there is no 5% check backwards: [H₃O⁺] is measured, not estimated (4b grey tag, decision board, key note 3). Why pKa is not pH: pH depends on this solution's concentration, pKa on the acid (4d). Why an amphiprotic ion goes one way: its two reactions with water compete, and the larger constant wins (5b, 5c). Why the Kb uses the Ka one proton up: accepting a proton turns the ion into its conjugate acid (5b, spoken), and Ka × Kb = Kw holds only for a conjugate pair (5d, spoken).
teaching.conversationalApproach: Weak acid questions give different data, and the data choose the method: a Ka and a concentration (estimate x, then check it was fair), a measured pH (run the table backwards), or an ion that can go either way (compare Ka with Kb). Q1 (hypochlorous acid) uses the shortcut and justifies it with the under-five-per-cent check; Q2 (chloroethanoic acid) tries the shortcut, sees the check fail because about a quarter ionises, and solves the full quadratic; Q3 (benzoic acid) goes from a measured pH to [H3O+], the equilibrium row, Ka and pKa; Q4 compares the two reactions of hydrogen carbonate and of dihydrogen phosphate with water, finding each Kb from the conjugate acid's Ka. Each question ends with its spoken, crossed classic mistake (no square root, keeping a failed shortcut, pKa equal to pH, Kb from the ion's own Ka), and the decision board chooses the method from the data.
teaching.openingDecision: Weak acid questions give you different data, and the data choose the method. A K a and a concentration? Estimate x, then check it was fair. A measured pH? Work backwards to K a. An ion that can give or take a proton? Compare its K a with its K b. Here are four HSC-style questions. Pause and try each one, then we'll work it through, one step at a time.
teaching.understandingCheck: Four, each 10 s with the countdown and every demand and condition visible (2a, 3a, 4a, 5a): concentrations, Ka values, the measured pH, 25 °C, "monoprotic" (Q2, Q3), all five constants in Q4 and Q4's three demands, including the equations. Nothing answer-bearing during the holds; the check strip dims.
teaching.curriculumScope: Syllabus (NSW Chemistry Stage 6, 2017, p53), as printed: "calculate pH, pOH, hydrogen ion concentration ([H+]) and hydroxide ion concentration ([OH–]) for a range of solutions (ACSCH102)" "calculate and apply the dissociation constant (Ka) and pKa (pKa = -log10 (Ka)) to determine the difference between strong and weak acids (ACSCH098)" "write ionic equations to represent the dissociation of acids and bases in water, conjugate acid/base pairs in solution and amphiprotic nature of some salts, for example: - sodium hydrogen carbonate - potassium dihydrogen phosphate" The route entry lists C6-IQ2-02 only. Q3 applies C6-IQ3-04 (Ka and pKa) and Q4 applies C6-IQ2-04 (the two named amphiprotic salts) with C10's Ka × Kb = Kw, so both are quoted. Practice and transfer only: the coverage rows stay with chem-m6-c06, c08 and c10; G02 adds practice rows, not first coverage. Root to decide whether the route entry adds C6-IQ3-04 and C6-IQ2-04 as practice actions. starts at the route's "Present unfamiliar weak-acid data and protect an attempt" and stops at its "Choose an approximation or full method, test the assumption and check pH". Four questions, each chosen by the data it gives: a Ka and a concentration where the shortcut passes; a Ka and a concentration where the 5% check fails and the full equation is solved; a measured pH, worked backwards to Ka and pKa; and the amphiprotic Ka-against-Kb item assigned here by the route review (`../../module6-route-review-claude.md`, Additions, 19 Oct: "Amphiprotic Ka against Kb (which way an amphiprotic ion reacts): C10 deferred it and C11 leaves it out. It goes to chem-m6-g02 (practice)."). Not here: weak bases (C08 worked one; no new method); buffers and Henderson-Hasselbalch (chem-m6-c11, the next video); salt pH calculations and hydrolysis of ions from one weak parent (chem-m6-c13, c14); polyprotic pH calculations (C10 decision: out); the pH of an amphiprotic salt solution (Q4 predicts acidic or basic only, with no number).

design.visualSystem: One practice board throughout, in the bio-m6-g01 layout: top-left the question card (stem, data and demands, as an exam prints them, with the tag "HSC-style question, written for HSCScience"), kept readable through the whole question; the working fills the right two thirds; a type badge top-right ("Ka given: shortcut", "Ka given: full equation", "pH given: backwards", "Amphiprotic: Ka against Kb"), hidden during each attempt because it names the method. When the walkthrough starts, the card shrinks to a strip and each given is underlined in amber in the question text at the cue where it is used (no givens card). A check strip on the far left carries three rows, "what data?", "is x small?", "does it make sense?", and ticks the row each scene uses; it dims to an outline during every countdown. Earlier questions are cleared before the next card writes on. Working follows the C08 and C10 staging: equation strip, the ICE table as one item (once filled, only its equilibrium row stays bright), the C08 check ruler (a long bar for c, a sliver for x, a dashed 5% line), one stage per line, earlier lines dimming, one kept chip into the next scene. Colour key from C08 and C10: H₃O⁺ teal, OH⁻ violet, whole weak-acid molecules amber-outlined, the acid's anion grey-violet, Ka values teal, pKa navy, Kb violet-tinted, meter readouts amber digits; amber is otherwise used only for underlined givens and the check. Clutter rule (owner): besides the question strip and the check strip, at most about three bright text items in the working area at once; each tag fades when the next cue lands.
design.transitionPlan: The heading writes on and three data chips fan out, one per cue; each question opens on a fresh board with the type badge hidden while the worded card writes, with the meter, baking soda or fertiliser plates small at its corner; the walkthrough shrinks the card to a strip, lights the type badge and underlines each given in amber as the ICE table, XRuler sliver, quadratic lines or KaFrac write one stage per line with earlier lines dimming; the two-reaction fork draws for each amphiprotic ion and shrinks to a grey thumbnail with its result chip; each classic mistake writes as a chip and takes a grey scribble cross; the check strip returns full size as the two-column decision board, row by row; scene crossfade with settle.

scenes.motionPurpose: The question card builds with every given visible and stays on screen; no answer cues appear; the countdown ring runs for 10 seconds after "Pause here to answer." (question 4: two amphiprotic ions)
scenes.onScreenChange: board clears. Type badge hidden. `m6-baking-soda-box-v1.png` and `m6-fertiliser-granules-v1.png` sit small at the card's upper right, with coded labels "NaHCO₃" and "KH₂PO₄". The card writes on: "Sodium hydrogen carbonate, NaHCO₃ (baking soda), and potassium dihydrogen phosphate, KH₂PO₄ (used in some fertilisers), dissolve in water to give the amphiprotic ions HCO₃⁻ and H₂PO₄⁻." Data block, one line each: "Ka(H₂CO₃) = 4.3 × 10⁻⁷", "Ka(HCO₃⁻) = 4.7 × 10⁻¹¹", "Ka(H₃PO₄) = 7.1 × 10⁻³", "Ka(H₂PO₄⁻) = 6.3 × 10⁻⁸", "Kw = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ (all at 25 °C)". Demands: "(a) For each ion, write an equation for its reaction with water as an acid, and as a base." "(b) Use Ka and Kb values to determine which reaction mainly occurs for each ion." "(c) Predict whether a solution of each salt is acidic or basic." Three answer boxes. Nothing answer-bearing (no arrows, no chains, no equations). **Countdown 10 seconds**; strip dims.
scenes.holdPurpose: 10 second answer-free countdown after "Pause here to answer."; the card stays on screen

scenes.visualReference: the card shrinks to a strip; type badge "Amphiprotic: Ka against Kb".
scenes.teachingReason: Two reactions, two constants: An amphiprotic ion runs two reactions with water, so compare their constants.
scenes.narrationCue: donating / four point seven times ten to the minus eleven / Accepting / conjugate acid / two point three times ten to the minus eight / basic
scenes.motionPurpose: On the spoken cues: The two-reaction fork draws: "HCO₃⁻" centre (split-outlined amber and violet, C06 style; grey tag "C06: amphi means both", which fades on "compare their constants"). On "donating" the right arrow draws with its full equation "HCO₃⁻(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ CO₃²⁻(aq) + H₃O⁺(aq)", which also writes into answer
scenes.onScreenChange: the card shrinks to a strip; type badge "Amphiprotic: Ka against Kb". The two-reaction fork draws: "HCO₃⁻" centre (split-outlined amber and violet, C06 style; grey tag "C06: amphi means both", which fades on "compare their constants"). On "donating" the right arrow draws with its full equation "HCO₃⁻(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ CO₃²⁻(aq) + H₃O⁺(aq)", which also writes into answer box (a). On "four point seven times ten to the minus eleven" "Ka(HCO₃⁻) = 4.7 × 10⁻¹¹" underlines, a teal chip "Ka = 4.7 × 10⁻¹¹" pins on the right arrow, and the arrow's equation reduces to the short label "donates → CO₃²⁻ + H₃O⁺". On "Accepting" the left arrow draws with its full equation "HCO₃⁻(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ H₂CO₃(aq) + OH⁻(aq)", which also writes into answer box (a). On "becomes carbonic acid" the mini chain "H₂CO₃ ⇄ HCO₃⁻ ⇄ CO₃²⁻" writes small with H₂CO₃ ringed (tag "one proton up"); on "conjugate acid" a C10-style bracket "conjugate pair" joins H₂CO₃ and HCO₃⁻. "Ka(H₂CO₃) = 4.3 × 10⁻⁷" underlines; on "two point three times ten to the minus eight" the mini chain dims and the line "Kb(HCO₃⁻) = Kw ÷ Ka(H₂CO₃) = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ ÷ 4.3 × 10⁻⁷ = 2.3 × 10⁻⁸" writes; a violet chip "Kb = 2.3 × 10⁻⁸" pins on the left arrow, the Kb line dims as the chip pins, and the left arrow's equation reduces to "accepts → H₂CO₃ + OH⁻". On "five hundred times" the left arrow thickens (tag "Kb ≈ 500 × Ka"). On "basic" answer boxes (b) and (c) fill "HCO₃⁻: Kb > Ka, mainly accepts" and "NaHCO₃: basic (OH⁻ formed)", and the ratio tag fades. Bright in the working area at any moment: the fork (centre ion, two arrows, their chips), one working item (the full equation being written, the mini chain or the Kb line) and at most one tag. Strip: "what data?" ticks.

scenes.onScreenChange: the HCO₃⁻ fork shrinks to a grey thumbnail with its result chip "accepts: basic". A new fork draws for "H₂PO₄⁻". On "Donating" the right arrow draws with its full equation "H₂PO₄⁻(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ HPO₄²⁻(aq) + H₃O⁺(aq)", which also writes into answer box (a). On "six point three times ten to the minus eight" "Ka(H₂PO₄⁻) = 6.3 × 10⁻⁸" underlines, the teal chip pins and the equation reduces to "donates → HPO₄²⁻ + H₃O⁺". On "Accepting" the left arrow draws with its full equation "H₂PO₄⁻(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ H₃PO₄(aq) + OH⁻(aq)", also into answer box (a). On "phosphoric acid" the mini chain "H₃PO₄ ⇄ H₂PO₄⁻ ⇄ HPO₄²⁻" writes small with H₃PO₄ ringed ("one proton up"); "Ka(H₃PO₄) = 7.1 × 10⁻³" underlines; on "one point four times ten to the minus twelve" the chain dims and "Kb(H₂PO₄⁻) = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ ÷ 7.1 × 10⁻³ = 1.4 × 10⁻¹²" writes; the violet chip pins, the Kb line dims and the left equation reduces to "accepts → H₃PO₄ + OH⁻". On "K a wins" the right arrow thickens (tag "Ka ≈ 45 000 × Kb"). On "acidic" answer boxes (b) and (c) add "H₂PO₄⁻: Ka > Kb, mainly donates" and "KH₂PO₄: acidic (H₃O⁺ formed)", and the ratio tag fades. Only then the strip's "does it make sense?" row ticks, with a grey tag "C06: baking soda neutralised acid" (the C06 hook, consistent with a basic solution). Revision 2: no `PKRuler` thumbnail and no pKb values (pKb is not taught in C10). Same clutter limit as 5b.

scenes.teachingReason: The classic mistake: The classic mistake is finding K b from the ion's own K a.

On "hydrogen phosphate" the caption "that's the Kb of HPO₄²⁻" writes under the cross. On "conjugate pair" the mini chain "H₃PO₄ ⇄ H₂PO₄⁻ ⇄ HPO₄²⁻" returns small and a
scenes.onScreenChange: the two fork thumbnails dim. A chip "Kb(H₂PO₄⁻) = Kw ÷ 6.3 × 10⁻⁸ = 1.6 × 10⁻⁷, so basic" writes on and, on "the classic mistake", takes a grey scribble cross. On "hydrogen phosphate" the caption "that's the Kb of HPO₄²⁻" writes under the cross. On "conjugate pair" the mini chain "H₃PO₄ ⇄ H₂PO₄⁻ ⇄ HPO₄²⁻" returns small and a C10-style bracket "conjugate pair" joins H₃PO₄ and H₂PO₄⁻.
